introduction_markdown:
Answer both questions beginning each answer on a new page in the answer booklet. Both answers carry equal marks.

Credit will be given for accuracy, correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.

Use blue ink only.

You are reminded of the necessity for orderly presentation of your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
*Using a tense suitable to your chosen topic, write an essay in French, of at least 140 and not more than 150 words, (not counting figures, words in brackets, abbreviations and names of people or places) on ONE of the following topics.*

*Credit will be given for the correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.*

*If you choose topic (b), your name must be Kassala and your address Lycée de Mololo.*

*If you choose topic (c), your essay must be based on the events in the pictures.*

*Off-topic material will earn no marks.*

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Tense chosen:** the passé composé for what happened this morning, with the imparfait to describe how the friend looked and felt. The text is a letter to the friend's father, so it has a place and date, a salutation, a body and a closing formula, and it is signed *Kassala* with the address *Lycée de Mololo* as required.

**Model essay** (148 words, counted with the heading and signature; 141 without the names of people and places and the figure)

Lycée de Mololo, le 12 mars

Monsieur,

Je vous écris pour vous raconter ce qui est arrivé ce matin à votre fils Paul. Sur le chemin de l'école, il a eu un malaise : il était pâle, il tremblait et il a fini par tomber. Il avait très chaud et il ne pouvait plus parler. Je me suis précipité vers lui pour le soutenir.

J'ai eu peur, mais j'ai gardé mon calme. Des passants se sont arrêtés et un commerçant a hélé un taxi. Nous avons emmené Paul à l'hôpital, où les infirmières l'ont installé.

Là, le médecin l'a examiné et lui a donné un traitement. C'était seulement un coup de chaleur, parce qu'il n'avait rien mangé ce matin-là. Quelques heures après, il allait mieux. Le médecin pense qu'il pourra rentrer demain, et vous pouvez venir le voir quand vous voulez.

Veuillez agréer, Monsieur, mes salutations respectueuses.

Kassala

**Notes**

The letter follows the three bullet points: the nature of the illness and how the friend reacted (paragraph 1), the writer's reaction and that of the people around (paragraph 2), what happened at the hospital and how it ended (paragraph 3). The name Kassala and the address Lycée de Mololo are imposed by the topic; names of people and places are not counted in the word limit.

**Marking criteria**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | Correct verb forms, agreements, spelling and accents; correct use of the tense chosen |
| Variety of expressions | Linking words (*d'abord*, *puis*, *finalement*, *heureusement*) and set phrases |
| Variety of verbs | Several different verbs instead of *être*, *avoir* and *faire* only |
| Vocabulary and idioms | Words and expressions suited to the topic; idioms used correctly |
| Relevance and length | All three bullet points covered; between 140 and 150 words |

**Common mistakes**

1. Forgetting the letter format (address, date, salutation, closing) or not using the imposed name and address.
2. Using the wrong register: the letter goes to a friend's father, so *vous* and a polite closing formula (*Veuillez agréer, Monsieur, ...*) are expected, not *tu* or *Cher papa*.
